fields.aka: Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya, Gaurāṅga, Gaura Hari, Gorā, Śacīnandana, Nimāi, Nimāi Paṇḍita, Viśvambhara, Caitanya, Lord Caitanya
fields.disappearance: 1455 Śaka, in His 48th year (1533; the Abhidhāna: 1534 CE), during saṅkīrtana in the temple of Ṭoṭā-Gopīnātha, Purī (Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura)

fields.aka: Nitāi, Nityānanda Rāma, Avadhūta, Kuvera (former name), Śrīla
fields.appearance: Māgha Śukla Trayodaśī (Nityānanda Trayodaśī), 1395 Śaka (1473/1474 CE), at Ekacakrā, Birbhum
fields.guru: Mādhavendra Purī (Abhidhāna; the Caitanya-bhāgavata shows Him revering Mādhavendra as His guru); Lakṣmīpati Tīrtha (Bhakti-ratnākara; Gauḍīya Maṭha); Īśvara Purī (Prema-vilāsa 24); Saṅkarṣaṇa Purī (Jīva Gosvāmī)
fields.notes:
Father: Hāḍāi Paṇḍita (Hāḍo Ojhā). Mother: Padmāvatī. Grandfather: Sundarāmalla Nakaḍi Bāḍurī, a Rāḍhī brāhmaṇa of the Śāṇḍilya gotra. Former name Kuvera; an avadhūta. Wives: Vasudhā and Jāhnavā. Children: Vīracandra (Vīrabhadra) and Gaṅgā. In Kṛṣṇa-līlā: Balarāma (Halāyudha). Described as the trunk of the tree of bhakti (CC 1.9.21). Pilgrimage until age 20; met Lord Caitanya at the house of Nandana Ācārya in Navadvīpa; delivered Jagāi and Mādhāi.

His guru: the Abhidhāna says Mādhavendra Purī (otherwise Lakṣmīpati); the Bhakti-ratnākara (Narahari Cakravartī) says He took dīkṣā from Lakṣmīpati Tīrtha; the Caitanya-bhāgavata (Vṛndāvana dāsa) shows Mādhavendra treating Him as a friend while He revered Mādhavendra as His guru; the Prema-vilāsa (24) says Īśvara Purī; Jīva Gosvāmī, Saṅkarṣaṇa Purī. A usual reconciliation: Lakṣmīpati Tīrtha the dīkṣā guru, Mādhavendra Purī guru in the wider sense.

In Kṛṣṇa-līlā: Saṅkarṣaṇa / Balarāma; as Ananta Śeṣa He becomes the couch, garments and ornaments of the Lord (Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 59-64).

Family (exact names): father Hadai Ṭhākura (Mukunda Ojha Haddipa Paṇḍita); mother Padmāvatī Devī; wives Vasudhā and Jāhnavā Devī (Mātā); father-in-law Suryadasa Paṇḍit; son Vīracandra (Vīrabhadra Gosvāmī); daughter Gaṅgā Devī; son-in-law Mādhava Ācārya.

The twelve gopālas (Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 126-132; exact names): Abhirāma Ṭhākura (Śrīdāmā), Sundarānanda Ṭhākura (Sudāmā), Dhananjaya (Vasudāmā), Gaurī Dāsa Paṇḍit (Subala), Kamalakara Pippalai (Mahābala), Uddhāraṇa Datta Ṭhākura (Subāhu), Maheśa Paṇḍita (Mahābāhu), Puruṣottama Dāsa (Dāma), Parameśvara Dāsa Ṭhākura (Arjuna), Kālīya Kṛṣṇa Dāsa Ṭhākura (Lavaṅga), Kholāvecā Śrīdhara (Kusumāsava).

Paramparā (Gauḍīya Sampradāya chart, 04-11-2026): dīkṣā from Lakṣmīpati Tīrtha according to the Gauḍīya Maṭha (disputed); other sources: Mādhavendra Purī. The tree had Saṅkarṣaṇa Purī (dīkṣā) and Lakṣmīpati Tīrtha (sannyāsa).

Disappearance: the date «8 October 1540» in this record has no source; the Abhidhāna and the Gauḍīya calendar do not give one.
